title: Why Does Your Road Car Have Race Car Parts?
description:
The small mirror above your windscreen was first made famous by a racing driver, at the very first Indianapolis five hundred, in nineteen eleven. Your brakes were proven at Le Mans. The paddles behind the steering wheel came from Formula One. Your everyday car is full of parts that were invented, tested or perfected in racing. Today, ten race car parts hiding in your road car, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:13 1. The rear view mirror
2:29 2. The disc brakes
3:44 3. The fuel injectors
5:06 4. The twin camshafts
6:27 5. The dual clutch gearbox
7:52 6. The paddle shifters
9:07 7. The carbon fibre
10:36 8. The rear spoiler
11:58 9. The smart suspension
13:13 10. The energy recovery
14:34 The verdict

- Peugeot L76, twin overhead camshafts, 1912-1913: Wikipedia, "Peugeot L76" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peugeot_L76
